title: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models
abstract: Studies fine-grained citations for attributed generation, aiming to connect generated claims to localized supporting evidence rather than attaching only coarse document-level references.

admission.reason: Topic words match F3, but the abstracted contribution is primarily learning/generating fine-grained grounded citations. It does not establish a distinct evaluation methodology for citation correctness or completeness beyond the stronger evaluation-focused candidates admitted in F3.

title: Correctness is not Faithfulness in RAG Attributions
abstract: Separates attribution correctness from attribution faithfulness in RAG, showing that a citation can support an answer while failing to reflect the evidence that actually influenced generation.

admission.reason: The distinction between attribution correctness and causal attribution faithfulness is conceptually useful, but the latter asks whether cited evidence actually influenced generation. msgloom's immediate Topic 10 requirement is evidential support, attribution correctness, and completeness; the admitted F3 papers more directly strengthen those evaluation capabilities.

title: Computing Reliability for Coreference Annotation
abstract: Develops a reliability methodology for structured linguistic annotation where disagreements can be partial and annotation units are not trivially commensurate.

admission.reason: This is transferable structured-annotation reliability work, but its coreference-specific treatment offers lower marginal value than the direct NLG/human-evaluation reliability papers admitted for F10. The identity is also UNCHECKED, so there is no reason to consume a reading slot when stronger VERIFIED alternatives cover the needed methodology.

title: Agreement is overrated: A plea for correlation to assess human evaluation reliability
abstract: Examines reliability assessment in NLG human evaluation and argues that inter-annotator agreement alone can be misleading; recommends considering agreement together with correlation measures.

admission.reason: Relevant to F10, but its central contribution about combining agreement and correlation is substantially overlapped by the more directly applicable modern agreement/abstention analysis admitted under F10. Given the UNCHECKED identity and limited marginal coverage, it does not justify another reading slot.

title: Human evaluation of automatically generated text: Current trends and best practice guidelines
abstract: Reviews human-evaluation practice in NLG and provides guidelines covering study design, execution, reporting, reliability, and reproducibility.

admission.reason: A broad best-practice review is relevant background for F10, but the candidate set already contains empirical papers on reproducibility, judge validation, abstention-aware agreement, retained human review, and representative sampling. Its incremental contribution is therefore too diffuse for this strict reading round, and its identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability
abstract: Foundational paper introducing a proper quadratic score for evaluating probabilistic forecasts, later known as the Brier score; directly relevant to empirical reliability and calibration evaluation.

admission.reason: The Brier score is foundational probabilistic-scoring machinery, but the candidate does not materially address language-task calibration, distribution shift, selective coverage, or evidence-conditioned reliability. The admitted QA-calibration paper is a substantially closer transfer target for F8, so this historical foundation does not justify a scarce reading slot.

title: QAFactEval: Improved QA-Based Factual Consistency Evaluation for Summarization
abstract: Improves question-answering-based factual consistency evaluation by systematically selecting and combining QA components for testing whether summary claims are supported by source documents.

admission.reason: This is a valid F1 factual-consistency evaluator, but its QA-based metric is additional methodological variation after admitting a localized evidence-span evaluator and a cross-dataset NLI meta-evaluation. The abstract does not show a distinct capability needed badly enough to justify another F1 reading slot.

title: QuestEval: Summarization Asks for Fact-based Evaluation
abstract: Uses question generation and question answering over source and summary to evaluate whether generated text preserves relevant source information and remains factually consistent.

admission.reason: QuestEval combines source/summary QA for relevance and factual evaluation, but the admitted Pyramid paper provides a more explicit semantic-unit treatment of completeness and the admitted F1 papers provide stronger source-grounded factuality coverage. Its marginal contribution is therefore insufficient for this strict round.
